findings.problem: All nine right-answer explanations open with a short affirmation before explaining: "YES, baker" (card 2), "THERE it is." (card 4), "MERCY, baker!" (card 6), "You got it, baker." (card 8), "Heavenly realms, friend!" (card 10), "Right, baker" (card 12), "GIFT!" (card 14), "That's it, friend." (card 16), "BEAUTIFUL, baker." (card 18). None of these is one of the listed reaction phrases. But the code already shows a right-answer reaction just before, so these may work as a second reaction. Because every right answer opens the same way, they may also be a formula.
findings.question: answer-explanations.md says "The explanation never includes a reaction" and lists the exact reaction phrases. Does that rule also cover short affirmations like "You got it, baker" or "YES, baker" at the start of a right-answer explanation? Or are those fine as long as they aren't the listed phrases?
